overview.about: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is the most important festival in Hinduism and is also celebrated by Jains, Sikhs and some Buddhists. Marked by rows of oil lamps (diyas), fireworks, sweets and family gatherings, it symbolises the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. It is a public holiday across India and in many countries with large South Asian communities.
overview.nextEvent: The next Diwali falls in autumn on the darkest night of the Hindu lunar month and is celebrated over about five days. Homes and streets glow with lamps and rangoli patterns, families exchange sweets and gifts, and fireworks light the night sky.

@graph.name: Diwali
@graph.description: Diwali is a five-day festival of lights observed by Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and some Buddhists, although its religious stories and local customs vary by community. In much of India, lamps, rangoli, sweets and family visits mark the new-moon night, while Lakshmi Puja is a central observance for many Hindu households. The 2026 main Diwali date is 8 November; it is a nationwide observance rather than an event held in one city or venue.
